entries.content:
Ashley Moulton

Healthcare Lead, Chrome Enterprise Ecosystem, Google

Special offer for healthcare organizations

Chrome Enterprise Premium offers enhanced protections for patient data.

Learn more

Healthcare is adopting AI quickly, and it's moving beyond chat. Clinical teams are starting to use AI agents that draft documentation, summarize charts, navigate web apps, and complete multi-step tasks on a clinician's behalf. Many of these agents work in the same place—the browser. As electronic health records (EHRs) and clinical apps move to the web, the browser is where clinicians, applications, patient data, and AI services meet. When clinicians or agents act inside a session, security teams need clear control over what they can access.

Healthcare systems frequently adopt a multi-vendor AI strategy, a flexibility that should be fully supported. Whether clinicians are using Gemini™ or an array of other web-based AI tools and extensions, Chrome Enterprise Premium secures data across the board to:

  • Guard sensitive data: Advanced DLP controls restrict unauthorized copying and pasting, form submission, printing, and screen capture of sensitive data—preventing patient data from leaking into unapproved AI prompts or browser extensions.
  • Maintain full operational visibility: Granular reporting and visibility into browser activity, extension usage, and data transfers help security teams uncover shadow AI and maintain internal oversight.
  • Govern extensions and web AIs consistently: Security policies and extension controls apply directly at the browser layer, so IT teams can manage permissions, block risky extensions, and enforce guardrails across every AI service without needing a separate harness for each tool.

Since we introduced new healthcare integrations in May, Chrome Enterprise has continued to invest in the healthcare ecosystem. Today we're sharing the next set of milestones that bring Chrome Enterprise to more clinical endpoints.

Chrome Enterprise is now compatible with IGEL® OS

As healthcare organizations accelerate the adoption of web-based clinical applications and AI-powered workflows, securing both the browser and the endpoint has become increasingly important. To address this, Chrome Enterprise is now compatible with IGEL® OS and soon available in the IGEL® Marketplace, allowing healthcare IT to easily deploy and manage the browser across IGEL OS™ endpoints, including shared workstations, nursing stations, and clinical carts.

This collaboration combines Google's enterprise-grade browser management and security capabilities with the IGEL Adaptive Secure Endpoint Platform,™ providing an immutable, centrally-managed endpoint foundation designed to reduce the attack surface and simplify IT operations. Through the IGEL App Portal and IGEL Universal Management Suite (UMS), organizations can streamline application deployment and endpoint governance, while the Google Admin console provides centralized browser policy and extension management.

Native browsing for flexible clinical endpoints with Citrix® UniconOS

Through our expanded collaboration with Citrix, healthcare systems can now run Chrome Enterprise natively on Citrix UniconOS endpoints. Clinicians get a fast, familiar experience on any device, while IT gains another flexible option for adding secure access and data protections across their clinical environments.

Expanding collaboration with Omnissa® for enhanced device trust

Many healthcare organizations use Omnissa Workspace ONE® and Omnissa Horizon® to manage, secure and deliver critical clinical applications. We're expanding our collaboration with Omnissa to bring zero-trust security and device posture assessment to healthcare environments. Building on May's integration, organizations can verify device health before clinicians reach critical applications.

Optimizing Epic® Workflows at the point of care

Beyond endpoint expansion, we are introducing new Chrome Enterprise capabilities that streamline clinic workflows, including support for silent printing and PDF updates for Epic® Hyperspace® for the web. This allows clinicians to route essential orders and wristbands directly to authorized printers, while native PDF rendering keeps protected health information strictly isolated within the active, managed session.

Scaling clinical technology with confidence

Together, these updates give IT and security teams the confidence to say yes to modern clinical technology, supporting the patient care experience—without giving up critical protections and control. As healthcare organizations continue deploying enterprise AI solutions like Gemini or managing a fast-growing ecosystem of third-party AI web apps and browser extensions, Chrome Enterprise provides the unified security, Data Loss Prevention (DLP), and governance layer needed to empower care teams with confidence.

To get started, explore Chrome Enterprise in the IGEL Marketplace, see how our latest updates support your Epic® and clinical workflows or visit our website or contact us today.

entries.content:
Bharath Sivaraman

Senior Product Manager

Even as sophisticated, new zero-day exploits continue to emerge, most cybersecurity incidents still start from the same common sources: an attacker locating and exploiting a fundamental, easily preventable cloud misconfiguration.

Organization Policy Service can help you secure resource configurations and set up security guardrails across your Google Cloud resource hierarchy. Using a catalog of over 100 predefined policies for many common cloud governance needs, as well as Custom Organization Policy, you can more easily set up boundaries with granular control over resources.

To help platform and security teams author, audit, and scale guardrails with greater speed and simplicity, we are introducing the general availability of our Organization Policy Model Context Protocol (MCP) server and natural-language constraint authoring powered by Gemini.

Managing Organization Policy with agents

Rather than forcing administrators to manually parse complex hierarchy chains, the Organization Policy MCP server offers tools that allow autonomous agents and pipelines to interact directly with Organization Policy. 

Using the Organization Policy MCP server, agents can assist administrators with posture audits, drift detection, and exemption management. Key capabilities include:

  • Constraint discovery: Tools like 'ListConstraints' and 'GetCustomConstraint' allow agents to understand the specific guardrails that apply to a project, folder, or organization.

  • Policy evaluation: The 'GetEffectivePolicy' tool calculates the effective policy after considering hierarchy inheritance and tag-based conditions. You can use this to verify if a configuration change will be compliant.

  • Manage policy: 'CreatePolicy' and 'CreateCustomConstraint' allow platform teams to manage guardrails via conversational workflows.

For example, you can combine your preferred coding agent with the Organization Policy MCP tools to create a custom dashboard to visualize the constraints applied to an organization and identify the folders and projects in the organization that have been exempted from the policy. You can also build custom agents and skills to streamline managing Organization Policy.

Figure 1: Custom dashboard created with Organization Policy MCP tools displaying enforced constraints

Figure 2: Visualize enforced constraints and identify exemptions with Organization Policy MCP tools.

Simplifying custom constraint authoring with Gemini

While the Organization Policy constraint catalog provides built-in managed constraints for common use cases, each organization has its own unique architectural standards. Custom Organization Policy enables customers to express these standards as a custom constraint and enforce them across supported services. 

Traditionally, administrators would write these rules in common expression language (CEL), which required a sharp understanding of Google Cloud resource schemas. Today, administrators can author custom Organization Policy in natural language through a Gemini prompt.

For example, you can prompt Gemini to require the use of agent-identity in Agent Runtime, to require that all agents deployed to Agent Runtime use an approved Agent Gateway, and to prevent users from disabling auto-upgrades on GKE, and refine custom constraints conversationally. 

To help ensure safe deployments, Gemini can also generate compliant and non-compliant test resource configurations that can help you test policy and validate in dry-run mode before enforcing the constraint.

Figure 3: Define custom constraints with a natural language prompt using Gemini

For targeted examples, the sample custom constraints library from Google Cloud Professional Services features pre-authored custom constraint samples based on CIS and PCI standards. Custom constraints are supported on a wide range of Google Cloud services including core AI and compute services including Agent Runtime, Agent Search, and Agent Studio on Gemini platform, Cloud Run, and Google Kubernetes Engine. 

Build faster, with confidence

Organization Policy provides proactive cloud governance of resource configurations on Google Cloud. It lets administrators enforce critical security guardrails so engineering teams can build and deploy quickly and securely.

With a growing catalog of built-in guardrails, autonomous tools for administrators, and the ability to tailor custom constraints across Google Cloud services, Organization Policy gives enterprises the control they need to scale safely.

Explore the Organization Policy documentation to learn more about resource governance in Google Cloud and set up your foundational guardrails.

entries.content:
Himanshu Mehra

Director, Product Management, Cloud Networking

Cross-Cloud Interconnect is expanding to connect to more of your workloads. We designed Google Cloud's Cross-Cloud Network to simplify and optimize how organizations connect and secure applications across cloud and on-premises environments. Last year, we launched partner Cross-Cloud Interconnect for AWS based on an open specification, turning complex cross-cloud network builds into a managed service that provisions in minutes. 

Today, we are extending partner Cross-Cloud Interconnect for last mile, starting in preview with Lumen Technologies, to bring that same simplicity and high-bandwidth connectivity to private clouds, on-premises data centers, neoclouds, and other clouds with expanded reach.

“The network needs to become as dynamic and easy to consume as the cloud itself. By bringing Google Cloud and Lumen connectivity together, we’re making it simpler for enterprises to connect their locations to the cloud with the performance and reliability they need. This is an important step toward a more programmable, cloud-like networking experience.” - Jim Fowler, EVP, Chief Technology & Product Officer, Lumen Technologies

Enterprise workloads and AI pipelines run across an increasing mix of public clouds, specialized neoclouds, private clouds, and on-premises sites. AI agents are also starting to assist with data and operational technology at customer branches, retail stores, and factory floors. Moving data reliably across these environments requires high-capacity private connectivity, but provisioning and managing that connectivity still relies on separate tools, providers, and operational models.

Cloud compute and storage capacity spin up in seconds, while connecting a physical site or private cloud can take weeks or months of manual quoting, cross-connect ordering, and routing configuration. Building solutions for high availability adds even more friction, as network engineers have to coordinate dual circuits across separate facilities, configure BGP failover, and manage encryption keys manually. With partner Cross-Cloud Interconnect for last mile and Lumen Technologies, you can leverage Lumen's expansive last-mile network to establish dedicated Layer 3 private connectivity to Google Cloud in minutes instead of months.

Programmable, resilient cloud connectivity

Partner Cross-Cloud Interconnect uses the open interconnect API specifications and provisioning process, so network teams can use one operational runbook for private cloud, neocloud, on-premises, and multicloud connections. 

  • On-demand connectivity to any environment: 1 to 50 Gbps scaling in minutes across public clouds, private clouds, AI neoclouds, and on-premises locations
  • Resilient and secure by default: pre-provisioned capacity across redundant routers in separate facilities/EADs, coordinated maintenance, and wire-speed MACsec encryption
  • Lower total cost of ownership (TCO): predictable flat-rate bandwidth tiers inclusive of Google Cloud data egress, eliminating idle physical port capacity and cross-connect fees

Choose the option that fits your needs

Partner Cross-Cloud Interconnect for CSPs: best for flexible, automated multicloud connectivity

  • Connect Google Cloud to providers like AWS or OCI without ordering dedicated physical ports or managing cross-connects

Partner Cross-Cloud Interconnect for last mile: best for expanding reach to private clouds, neoclouds, on-premises sites, and multicloud environments

  • Leverage partner last-mile networks, starting with Lumen, to connect your private clouds, neoclouds, data centers, and other cloud locations without waiting on long provisioning lead times

Availability

Partner Cross-Cloud Interconnect for last mile is available in preview in us-east4 (Northern Virginia) with Lumen Technologies, with additional regions coming soon.

To join in the preview, express your interest via this form, or contact your Google Cloud or Lumen account team. You can also read the Lumen announcement to learn more.

entries.content:
The Google Cloud Data Analytics, BI, and Database teams

Recent product news and updates from our data analytics, database and business intelligence teams.

November 9 - November 13

  • Bringing conversational analytics to Gemini with Data Cloud connectors: Data Cloud connectors in Gemini are now in preview, enabling knowledge workers to query live enterprise data using natural language directly within tools like Google Docs, Gmail, and Google Slides. The capability connects across BigQuery, Looker, Spanner, AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, and Cloud SQL without requiring data movement, grounded by Knowledge Catalog semantic models under user-identity IAM governance. Read the announcement blog.

  • Direct Apache Iceberg access in AlloyDB enables unified lakehouse querying: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL now supports direct querying of Apache Iceberg tables stored in Cloud Storage without requiring ETL pipelines or data duplication. Transactional applications can join operational data with analytical lakehouses in real time using standard PostgreSQL queries, accelerating cross-system analysis while maintaining complete relational integrity. Together with AlloyDB sync and lakehouse federation, you now have three integration approaches to choose from, depending on your use case. Read the launch blog.

  • AlloyDB Express delivers instant scale-to-zero PostgreSQL for developer prototyping: AlloyDB Express is now available, providing a lightweight, fast-provisioning PostgreSQL environment tailored for developers, testing, and AI coding agents like Antigravity. It scales to zero when idle to minimize costs while maintaining full PostgreSQL compatibility, allowing engineering teams to transition prototype workloads to production AlloyDB instances when ready. AlloyDB Express offers a free tier, with easy-to-understand pricing for higher usage. Read the announcement blog.

  • Carwow unifies its data foundation with BigQuery, Knowledge Catalog, and Looker to scale AI innovation: Europe's largest online car-changing marketplace migrated to BigQuery, Knowledge Catalog, and Looker to establish a governed single source of truth and enable trusted self-service analytics across the business. Paired with Gemini, Carwow automated vehicle document verification and PII redaction to save £2 million annually while cutting MLOps deployment cycles from months to weeks. Watch the Carwow customer story video.

  • Geospatial Analytics Playground enables natural-language exploration of BigQuery maps datasets: Google Maps Platform launched the Geospatial Analytics Playground, a natural-language evaluation environment built on top of Places Insights, Roads Management Insights, and Street View Insights datasets in BigQuery. Powered by Gemini, the open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK), and modular agent skills, the playground lets teams test spatial queries and validate dataset coverage without upfront spatial engineering. Read the announcement blog.

November 2 - November 6

  • BigQuery observability for data agents is now generally available: Data teams can now monitor the performance, adoption, latency, and cost of BigQuery data agents and their multi-turn conversations using Google Cloud Observability. This capability provides production-grade visibility into agent execution traces, usage volume, and query behavior so organizations can scale conversational analytics with confidence. Review the BigQuery release notes.

  • BigQuery change history and continuous queries for Apache Iceberg managed tables are now GA: BigQuery change history and continuous queries are now generally available for Lakehouse for Apache Iceberg managed tables. You can use the APPENDS table-valued function to track row additions over a specific time range and run continuous queries to read incoming data from and write output rows to Apache Iceberg managed tables. Review the BigQuery release notes.

  • BigQuery Data Engineering Agent adds support for BigQuery AI and ML functions: The BigQuery Data Engineering Agent now supports BigQuery AI, ML, and object functions and statements directly inside generated Dataform SQLX pipelines and agent instruction files. Paired with new folder-based Git repository integration in BigQuery Studio, data engineers can build, version, and automate AI-enriched data pipelines faster. Review the BigQuery release notes.

  • AlloyDB for PostgreSQL introduces AI-powered SQL tuning in preview: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL added the ai.tune_sql function in Public Preview. The function combines AI models with query execution plans and runtime statistics to automatically recommend query rewrites, missing indexes, vacuum operations, and database flag adjustments. Review the AlloyDB release notes.

  • Zero-downtime embedding model upgrades in AlloyDB AI: A new technical guide demonstrates how to upgrade vector embedding models in AlloyDB AI without disrupting production traffic. Using automatic embeddings alongside ScaNN vector indexes, engineering teams can transition to newer embedding models in the background while keeping semantic search and RAG applications online. Read the blog.

  • Shrink Cloud SQL for SQL Server storage disks with minimal downtime using Database Migration Service: A new technical guide demonstrates how to reclaim underutilized storage and reduce infrastructure costs on Cloud SQL for SQL Server instances using Database Migration Service (DMS). This workflow migrates databases to right-sized target disks with continuous replication so teams can downsize over-provisioned storage with minimal cutover downtime. Read the blog.

  • Dataflow Streaming Engine adds latency tiers and scheduled autoscaling: Dataflow introduced new horizontal autoscaling controls for Streaming Engine jobs, allowing teams to select low, medium, or high latency tiers to tune backlog sensitivity. Engineers can also configure recurring autoscaling schedules to adjust minimum and maximum worker counts or utilization targets during predictable traffic windows. Review the Dataflow release notes.

  • Spanner adds ON DELETE SET NULL foreign key actions across GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL: Spanner now supports the ON DELETE SET NULL referential action on foreign keys for both GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL dialects. When a referenced parent row is deleted, Spanner automatically updates the referencing child columns to NULL, simplifying schema migrations and relational integrity management. Review the Spanner release notes.

October 26 - October 30

  • LookML metadata indexing in Knowledge Catalog is now generally available: LookML models, Explores, Views, and join logic now continuously sync into the Knowledge Catalog context graph. This integration provides turnkey grounding for Gemini Enterprise and custom AI agents with deterministic business math, paired with end-to-end lineage tracing from underlying BigQuery tables directly to individual Looker dashboard tiles. Read the announcement blog.

  • Best Buy accelerates self-service insights with conversational analytics in BigQuery: Best Buy deployed conversational data agents directly against BigQuery to empower retail teams with multi-turn natural language exploration. The implementation reduces reliance on manual SQL and dedicated engineering queues, accelerating strategic planning and forecasting cycles while preserving enterprise governance and data protections validated against historical sales records. Explore the Best Buy customer story.

  • Myer accelerates retail insights with BigQuery data agents and Gemini: Leading department store Myer rolled out conversational data agents in BigQuery across 50+ retail analytics projects. Powered by Gemini, the solution enables commercial and merchandising teams to analyze store performance, stock levels, and customer trends using plain English, speeding up decision-making and reducing backlog requests for data teams. Read the Myer case study.

  • Rightmove speeds real estate analytics and predictive forecasting with Looker: The UK's top property portal unified its business analytics on Looker and BigQuery, delivering 4x faster reporting for 400+ team members and cutting meeting prep from hours to minutes. In addition, Rightmove built forecasting models that predict lead volume within 2–4.5% of actual results, while piloting Conversational Analytics in Looker. Read the Rightmove customer story.

  • BigQuery adds AI.TRANSLATE and AI.CHUNK_DOCUMENT for in-database text and RAG pipelines: BigQuery introduced two native generative AI capabilities to simplify unstructured data workflows directly within SQL. The 

    AI.TRANSLATE
    function enables multilingual translation across Neural Machine Translation and Translation LLMs, while the 
    AI.CHUNK_DOCUMENT
    table-valued function partitions unstructured text into semantically coherent segments optimized for vector embeddings and RAG pipelines. Review the BigQuery release notes.

  • AlloyDB adds in-database ai.extract and ai.classify functions to accelerate operational AI: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL introduced two new AI functions, 

    ai.extract
    and 
    ai.classify,
    in Public Preview, allowing developers to extract structured entities and categorize unstructured text directly inside SQL queries without external inference pipelines. These functions add to existing AlloyDB AI capabilities such as summarizing, generating, and filtering data with AI. Review the AlloyDB release notes.

  • AlloyDB Omni Web UI is generally available for centralized hybrid database management: The AlloyDB Omni Web UI is now generally available, providing a centralized graphical interface to manage hybrid and on-premises PostgreSQL deployments. Database administrators can monitor multi-cluster topologies, inspect columnar engine metrics, diagnose slow queries with Query Insights, and verify AI model connectivity across their database fleet. Review the AlloyDB Omni release notes.

  • Cloud Spanner adds approximate aggregate functions for high-speed analytics at scale: Cloud Spanner now supports approximate aggregate functions across both GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL dialects. Powered by HyperLogLog++ sketches, these functions generate fast statistical estimates for distinct count metrics with minimal compute overhead, accelerating analytical queries and reporting dashboards across petabyte-scale operational datasets. Review the Cloud Spanner release notes.

  • Knowledge Catalog introduces self-learning context enrichment and Knowledge Studio (Preview): Knowledge Catalog's enrichment agent now learns from agent and user interactions and from sources such as playbooks, code repositories, and business documents to find and fix missing or outdated context, which teams can package into reusable context sets. Knowledge Studio, the new studio experience in Knowledge Catalog, lets context engineers and data stewards explore their data estate conversationally, navigate a visual context graph, and review changes before they reach users and agents. Based on internal benchmarks, grounding agents in Knowledge Catalog makes them nearly 4x more accurate, with up to 33% lower latency and using up to 75% fewer tokens. Read the launch blog.

  • Knowledge Catalog now grounds AI agents in the semantic models you already trust (GA): Knowledge Catalog natively ingests semantic models and metric definitions from Looker LookML, BigQuery Graph, dbt MetricFlow, Snowflake Semantic Views, Databricks Metric Views, and SAP Core Schema Notation, and connects them with lineage, data quality, and access controls in a single context graph. Gemini Enterprise, BigQuery conversational analytics, and custom agents retrieve a metric's trusted formula, verified join path, and backing table in one context call, without moving data or rewriting business logic. Read the launch blog.

October 19 - October 23

  • BigQuery introduces column aliases in GoogleSQL and cross-region table copy GA

    GoogleSQL in BigQuery now supports column aliases in 

    SELECT
    and 
    WHERE
    clauses (GA opt-in), avoiding nested subqueries and simplifying migrations from Snowflake and Teradata. Cross-region table copying is also now generally available to streamline regional data replication and disaster recovery. Review the BigQuery release notes.

  • Conversational analytics in BigQuery expands to Canada and adds CSV/PDF export

    Conversational analytics in BigQuery is now available in Montréal (

    northamerica-northeast1
    ) and Toronto (
    northamerica-northeast2
    ) to support Canadian data residency requirements. You can also now export agent responses — including text, tables, charts, and citations — directly to CSV or PDF (GA). Learn more about conversational analytics in BigQuery.

  • AlloyDB Omni 18.4.0 is now GA with Advanced Query Insights and external KMS support

    AlloyDB Omni 18.4.0 brings PostgreSQL 18.4 to self-hosted and multi-cloud environments, adding the 

    google_insights_v2
    extension for granular query execution and wait-event diagnostics. It also adds Thales CipherTrust Manager support for Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) alongside HashiCorp Vault. Explore the AlloyDB Omni release notes.

  • Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL adds managed connection pooling and Private Service Connect defaults

    Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL now supports enabling built-in managed connection pooling on existing Private Service Connect (PSC) instances to scale high-concurrency workloads. PSC is also now the default private IP option for new Cloud SQL instances in new projects to simplify cross-project networking. Review Cloud SQL updates.

  • Customer momentum: Unico prevents over $5B in fraud on Google's Agentic Data Cloud

    Digital identity platform Unico migrated from Databricks Spark/Scala clusters to BigQuery and Spanner at the core of its data architecture. Unifying real-time transaction streams with petabyte-scale analytics enabled low-latency identity verification that has prevented over $5 billion in fraud. Read the Unico case study.

  • Developer guide: Getting started with Looker Data Apps

    Following the debut of Looker Data Apps in preview, a new walkthrough on the Google Developer Community shares practical patterns for building prompt-driven applications inside Looker. Read the guide on the Google Developer Community.

October 12 - October 16

  • Looker Data Apps are now in Preview to build and host interactive, agent-generated applications natively inside Looker

    Generated using natural language prompts, the Antigravity CLI, or Claude Code, these interactive web applications, natively hosted inside Looker, transform business reporting into operational systems of action. Users can test scenarios, adjust parameters, and trigger workflows in downstream platforms while inheriting LookML semantic modeling, row-level security, and access controls with no runtime LLM token costs. Read the announcement blog.

  • Build end-to-end data science pipelines with the Data Agent Kit

    Following the general availability of the Data Agent Kit, a new end-to-end walkthrough demonstrates how data teams can build, test, and schedule machine learning pipelines directly from their preferred code editors. Explore the walkthrough and codelab.

  • Manage dashboard agents as code to bring CI/CD and version control to LookML dashboards

    Data teams can now declare agent parameters, configurations, and prompt instructions alongside dashboard files in code. This integration enables standard developer workflows for conversational BI, including Git version control, peer review, branching, and automated CI/CD validation before agent modifications reach production end users. Read the technical guide on the Google Developer Community.

  • Simplify AI search with native AlloyDB hybrid search and Reciprocal Rank Fusion

    AlloyDB for PostgreSQL simplifies hybrid search architectures by combining vector similarity search and keyword BM25 retrieval within a unified database engine. Using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), developers can merge lexical scoring and semantic embeddings into a single ranked result without writing a complex SQL query. This unified approach removes the operational overhead of running and synchronizing external search engines alongside operational databases for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and search applications.Explore hybrid search in AlloyDB.

October 5 - October 9

  • Data Agent Kit is now generally available to bring Google Data Cloud to any coding agent

    Data Agent Kit provides a free collection of Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools and Google-authored agent skills that connect more than 15 Google Data Cloud services directly to coding agents across VS Code, Antigravity, Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex. This release expands support for developers and data practitioners to inspect schemas, author queries, and build end-to-end data pipelines in natural language directly from their IDE or CLI. Read the announcement blog.

  • Spanner Omni is now generally available for deploy-anywhere, multi-model workloads

    Spanner Omni brings Spanner's distributed SQL, graph, vector, and key-value capabilities to any environment, including on-premises data centers, other public clouds via Kubernetes or VMs, and local developer laptops. Organizations can build and run multi-model applications with consistent APIs and query engines across hybrid and multi-cloud footprints while seamlessly scaling to managed Spanner on Google Cloud. Read the launch blog and explore how Spanner also removed cumulative mutation limits for DML transactions.

  • AlloyDB delivers PostgreSQL for agents and native BM25 hybrid search

    We announced PostgreSQL for agents in AlloyDB, introducing an agentic database architecture engineered for real-time data access at agent scale with workload isolation. In addition, native BM25 ranking is now in Preview for AlloyDB and Cloud SQL, allowing developers to combine keyword search and vector embeddings directly in PostgreSQL without maintaining an external search engine. For hybrid deployments, the AlloyDB Omni RPM Orchestrator is now generally available, and you can dive deeper in our new Build AI apps and agents with AlloyDB eBook.

  • Lakehouse runtime catalog adds regional endpoints across 22 regions and GA support for flexible column names

    Lakehouse runtime catalog regional endpoints are now live across 22 Google Cloud regions across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and the Middle East, supporting both the Apache Iceberg REST catalog endpoint and the Apache Hive catalog endpoint to help customers meet strict data residency and sovereignty requirements. In addition, flexible column names for Apache Iceberg tables are now generally available by default across Iceberg external tables and managed tables, enabling seamless querying of columns containing spaces, hyphens, and Unicode characters. We also announced the Preview of cross-cloud caching and connections for the borderless Lakehouse.

  • Unlock predictive and agent-ready insights with BigQuery augmented analytics TVFs, TabFM, and identity columns

    BigQuery introduced augmented analytics table-valued functions (TVFs): six built-in functions that automate metric diagnostics, trend analysis, and pattern discovery directly where your data lives and integrate as skills for AI agents. We also introduced TabFM in BigQuery to bring tabular foundation model capabilities to predictive analytics, alongside BigQuery identity columns to automatically generate sequential surrogate keys and simplify data warehouse pipelines.

  • Dataflow adds Pause/Resume and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU support for large-scale AI workloads

    New Dataflow capabilities make it easier to run high-throughput streaming and batch AI pipelines at scale, including Pause/Resume job controls and support for NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. And for teams running Apache Spark workloads, learn how to mitigate compute stockouts and maximize availability using flexible VMs.

  • Unlock up to 3x higher QPS and microsecond latency with Memorystore for Valkey 9.1

    Memorystore for Valkey 9.1 is now available, delivering up to 3x higher queries per second (QPS) and microsecond-level caching latencies to accelerate high-throughput applications and real-time AI agent state management. Read the blog.

  • Customer momentum across Google Data Cloud — Yahoo, PayPal, Surescripts, Airwallex, and Lucius AI

    Organizations across industries are scaling their data and AI foundations on Google Data Cloud. Yahoo uses flexible VMs in Managed Service for Apache Spark to reduce provisioning failures by 85%, while PayPal migrated mission-critical analytics workloads to Managed Service for Apache Spark to scale and reduce operational overhead. On the database front, Surescripts migrated 30.5 billion annual healthcare transactions to AlloyDB with 99.998% uptime, Airwallex manages more than 5,000 databases with 99.99% availability on Cloud SQL with a team of four DBAs, and Lucius AI runs a 210,000-tender global platform on AlloyDB and MCP with 47x faster ScaNN vector search.

September 7 - September 10

  • Pub/Sub SMTs can now AI Inference your Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform models!

    Pub/Sub AI Inference SMTs allow you to apply inference on an incoming stream of events using models hosted in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. The model’s prediction is appended to your event, making it available for downstream processing in your data warehouse (like BigQuery) or operational database (like BigTable). This feature, now generally available, can dramatically simplify or enhance anomaly detection systems you are operating. 

  • PostgreSQL Source Connector is now generally available in Managed Service for Apache Kafka!

    Managed Service for Apache Kafka’s PostgreSQL connector allows customers to capture changes from their PostgreSQL database and ingest them into their Kafka infrastructure with low latency. This source connector is compatible withCloud SQL for Postgres, AlloyDB, and self-managed PostgreSQL databases. Try this along with our entire portfolio of managed connectors, including MirrorMaker 2.0, BigQuery, Cloud Storage, and Pub/Sub! E-mail kafka-hotline@google.com if you have questions or feedback!

  • Pause-on-failure for Dataflow batch jobs is GA

    Dataflow pause-on-failure enables you to preserve the state of a batch Dataflow job before it fails. By pausing your Dataflow job, you can address issues that are external to the pipeline and resume processing without losing completed work. This helps you better manage resource costs and improve job reliability when you face temporary outages or capacity constraints.

  • The insertAll API is now the BigQuery Storage Write API (REST)

    The legacy insertAll streaming API is now rebranded as the BigQuery Storage Write API (REST). By dropping the "legacy" label, developers can confidently build long-term HTTP-based streaming workflows. This stateless JSON-over-HTTPS endpoint offers a lightweight alternative to heavy gRPC libraries—ideal for serverless web apps, IoT telemetry, and AI logging. The transition is seamless for existing users, requiring zero code changes and offering 100% backward compatibility. However, the Storage Write API (gRPC) version remains the recommended standard for high-throughput, continuous pipelines.

August 31 - September 4

  • Stateful processing is available in BigQuery continuous queries in Preview

entries.content:
Andre Alfred

Sr. Director, Cloud Security Threat Operations

Modern security operations centers (SOCs) face an ongoing pipeline dilemma. While ingesting comprehensive endpoint telemetry is non-negotiable for defense, conventional delivery paths often drive up transfer overhead and alert latency. As attackers operate at machine speed, any unnecessary friction in how data moves from endpoints to the SOC can leave teams without the insight they need to respond to attacks in real time.

Addressing this requires optimizing the data pipeline at the integration layer. Rather than routing telemetry through complex intermediary cloud buckets that require ongoing maintenance and introduce costly processing delays, engineering teams need a streamlined delivery architecture. By eliminating architectural bottlenecks and optimizing data transit, security operations and IT leaders can significantly compress ingest latency, lower operational overhead, and give analysts near-instant visibility where it matters most.

Google Cloud and SentinelOne collaborated to solve this scaling challenge with a fundamentally re-architected integration. As a Google Unified Security Recommended endpoint detection and response (EDR) partner, SentinelOne pairs with Google Security Operations through direct integration and streamlined data schemas, delivering essential endpoint telemetry visibility to Google Security Operations detection and agentic SOC pipelines while significantly reducing the total cost of ownership of the integration.

What’s at stake?

For enterprise customers, every minute of telemetry latency can increase the blast radius of an active intrusion. When detection pipelines take half an hour to surface adversary activity, incident response transitions from active mitigation to retrospective damage control.

For the broader security community and IT leadership, inefficient ingestion pipelines can impact budget and compute resources. Retaining bulky, unoptimized telemetry in intermediate staging environments diverts resources away from strategic security initiatives and saddles engineering teams with unneeded infrastructure debt.

Technical highlights and capabilities

The re-engineered integration between Google Cloud and SentinelOne introduces six dedicated engineering workstreams designed to remove ingestion bottlenecks and reduce data overhead without sacrificing detection fidelity:

  • Significant event size reduction: A modernized EDR data schema greatly reduces the average event size, preserving full analytical fidelity and reducing downstream compute load for agentic workflows.

  • Direct Google API ingestion: SentinelOne directly streams events into Google Security Operations with APIs, eliminating intermediate cloud storage hops and associated storage fees.

  • Reduced streaming latency: Removing the requirement for intermediate cloud storage makes data available for detection, investigative, and agentic workflows in Google Security Operations in near real-time.

  • Precision telemetry scoping: Integrated SentinelOne Cloud Funnel filters allow further flexibility to customize telemetry sent to Google Security Operations.

  • Unified alerts API and Mandiant alignment: Parsers, alert models, and SOAR playbooks were engineered alongside Mandiant Incident Response and Managed Defense teams to support automated host isolation, full-disk deep visibility scans, malware extraction, and artifact enrichment directly from Google Security Operations.

  • Industry-validated partnership: Named Google Threat Intelligence's Intel Partner of the Year at Google Cloud Next.

Transform your SOC ingestion today

Modern defense requires direct action, not delayed transit. By cutting out unnecessary staging layers and streaming directly via APIs, your security team gains the speed needed to outpace modern threats while protecting your budget.

Targeted for phased delivery by end of year, initial rollouts are prioritizing customers using Mandiant Managed Defense and Mandiant Threat Defense. Contact your Google Cloud or SentinelOne account team today to evaluate your current telemetry pipeline, schedule a technical architecture review, and reserve early access for your environment.

entries.summary: Gartner has named Google a Leader, positioned furthest in vision, in its first-ever Magic Quadrant for Data Lakehouse Platforms. entries.content:
Sirish Chandrasekaran

VP, Product Strategy & Growth, Data Cloud

Gaurav Saxena

Director, Product Management

Gartner has named Google a Leader, positioned furthest in vision, in its first-ever Magic Quadrant for Data Lakehouse Platforms. In our opinion, this recognition validates a fundamental shift our customers are experiencing every day: In the agentic era, the enterprise lakehouse is no longer a passive data repository, but a foundation where agents reason and act across all your data.

The lakehouse originally emerged to bring data warehouse reliability to open, low-cost storage, but the benchmark defining the category is now shifting. Leading enterprises are moving rapidly from static reporting to autonomous AI agents that monitor operations, flag anomalies, and execute business workflows in real time. To support that shift, organizations need a platform where thousands of agents can read, reason, and act continuously across enterprise data without having to move that data first. Traditional, fragmented data stacks burdened by brittle pipelines, duplicated storage, and disjointed governance simply were not designed for the scale, performance, and latency required for agentic-scale workloads.

We engineered our borderless Lakehouse at every layer of the stack to eliminate this complexity and hidden cost. Specifically designed for agents to reason across petabyte-scale data, the borderless Lakehouse unifies your data estate across clouds, data platforms, and SaaS applications so you can ground agents in governed business context and bring Gemini directly to your data. This allows your teams to move from managing infrastructure to orchestrating business outcomes.

Activate your global data footprint in place

For most organizations, the biggest barrier to scaling AI is that enterprise data lives everywhere, spanning multiple clouds, operational databases, and SaaS platforms. Moving all of that data into a single physical location is slow, expensive, and introduces governance risk.

Our borderless Lakehouse acts as the bridge across your distributed environment to activate your data. Built on open Apache Iceberg, it connects your multi-cloud, SaaS, and operational data into a single governed fabric. Organizations can start analyzing datasets across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud  immediately without costly data copies or complex migrations, benefitting from:

  • Openness without performance trade-offs: Run analytics and AI across BigQuery and Managed Service for Apache Spark directly on open Iceberg tables with similar price-performance as native storage.
  • High-speed cross-cloud economics: Establishing private, high-speed paths to AWS and Azure is simple and cost-effective through Cross-Cloud Interconnect and intelligent caching. By caching only the active data blocks your queries touch, the lakehouse serves repeated lookups locally, protecting data residency and eliminating variable egress fees.
  • Vertically integrated security and governance: Keeping data protected wherever it resides is non-negotiable. Credential vending in Lakehouse runtime catalog helps ensure security policies travel directly with your agents wherever your data resides.

German banking leader Commerzbank built its AI strategy on our borderless Lakehouse and Apache Iceberg to deploy AI agents across contact centers and marketing while satisfying strict European banking regulations. A unified foundation now powers AI across the bank. The marketing team reduced campaign production times from weeks to days and empowered contact center agents with verified next steps in seconds.

Agents need business context, not just access

An autonomous agent is only as accurate as the business context it understands. The lakehouse bridges the gap between agents and enterprise data, automatically harvesting metadata directly from your storage layers and passing it to your context engines. The Lakehouse runtime catalog integrates directly with Knowledge Catalog, which acts as your universal context engine for your enterprise data. It autonomously aggregates and curates metadata and semantic context from all your sources, within and outside Google, enriches them to extract meaning, and serves this unified context to all the agents that you build and use. Key Knowledge Catalog capabilities include:

  • Unified aggregation across the enterprise: A single, governed semantic layer prevents metric drift across multi-cloud assets. With the general availability of expanded aggregation in Knowledge Catalog, organizations can unify metadata, metrics, and business logic across Looker, dbt, and BigQuery in one plane.
  • Turnkey agent grounding: Anchoring agents in verified business logic accelerates development and builds trust. Gemini grounded with Knowledge Catalog and context sets, both in preview, let teams package curated metrics and instructions into token-efficient bundles that agents consume via standard APIs and Model Context Protocol.
  • No-code context optimization: Delivering only the most relevant context reduces latency, lowers token costs, and prevents expensive reasoning loops. With a new studio experience in Knowledge Catalog, in preview, data stewards get an agentic-first, no-code environment to resolve definition gaps and securely govern the exact context that agents are authorized to access.

Bloomberg Media grounded their conversational queries directly in the Knowledge Catalog semantic layer, achieving a 63% improvement in query accuracy and eliminating hallucinations across their business teams.

Business context is only half the equation. Because agents act rather than just analyze, your analytical lakehouse and operational databases have to behave as one system. That is why BigQuery, Managed Service for Apache Spark, Spanner, and AlloyDB are built to work together, making the borderless Lakehouse the data foundation for the entire Agentic Data Cloud.

Empowering practitioners with an agentic lakehouse

Unlocking the full potential of your lakehouse requires transforming how people work with data. Historically, data engineers, data scientists, and business users operated in disconnected silos. The lakehouse acts as the collaborative connective tissue by integrating directly with Gemini, allowing you to build, test, and operate AI agents directly on top of your unified lakehouse data.

  • Intent-driven workflows for technical teams: With the Data Agent Kit, data practitioners can write code, build notebooks, and run ML models directly from their preferred IDEs and CLIs using simple text prompts. Instead of writing boilerplate code from scratch, teams can use pre-built agentic skills and MCP tools to build complex data pipelines and work seamlessly across 15+ Google Cloud data services
  • Proactive and personalized insights for business users: Conversational analytics gives business users trusted answers in plain language, without waiting on data teams to build custom reports. One-click publishing extends this, instantly turning approved technical models into conversational tools, allowing employees to ask plain-language questions, run accurate reports, and safely ground custom agents in daily workflows without any coding experience.

PayPal connected their Looker semantic models directly to AI agents using these capabilities, allowing business intelligence teams to define metric models once so that 5,000 employees could query live data with near 100% accuracy, accelerating insights by 50%.

Bringing AI-powered engines to the Lakehouse

To make decisions that impact your business in real time, AI agents need to run complex reasoning loops directly where your data lives. We bring Google's leading artificial intelligence and high-performance processing engines directly into open table formats, enabling you to extract massive value without the complexity of duplicating data. Consider the following use cases:

  • Running analytics at unprecedented scale: Driving real-time actions over petabytes of open data requires highly optimized compute. In BigQuery we've made queries over 40% faster while cutting query processing cost by more than 50% through intelligent optimizations like fluid scaling and built-in workload acceleration, while our Lightning Engine for Apache Spark runs open-format Spark workloads with an over 3x price-performance advantage over the leading alternative.
  • In-place AI and machine learning: With TabFM in preview, business teams can generate instant predictive insights on tabular data through simple SQL queries, while TimesFM 3.0 in BigQuery provides advanced multivariate forecasting over existing data.
  • Cost-effective agent-scale data processing: Agents query data continuously and in short bursts, so paying for idle compute quickly adds up. BigQuery fluid scaling introduces per-second billing with no minimum duration, removing the costly one-minute minimum to deliver up to 34% in compute cost savings.

Maximize efficiency at scale without cost spirals

Google Cloud's borderless Lakehouse redefines enterprise AI economics by delivering compounding savings across compute, AI processing, and token consumption. As agents apply AI across millions of rows, token spend can quickly become a very large line item. Knowledge Catalog prevents expensive token consumption by filtering and delivering only the precise metadata and metrics required for each prompt, avoiding the need to send massive, unorganized datasets to your LLMs, significantly reducing token consumption. BigQuery AI adds built-in token controls that let teams estimate usage before a query runs, set firm limits, and automatically switch to smaller, more efficient models through an optimized mode. The result is BigQuery's cost-optimized AI functions use 230x fewer tokens compared to row by row gen AI processing.

What’s next?

To learn more about our placement and how we think we can accelerate your data journey, download the complimentary 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Lakehouse Platforms report.

entries.content:
Paul Ramsey

Product Manager, AI for AlloyDB & Cloud SQL

Transactional databases store vast amounts of unstructured text — clinical notes, customer reviews, support tickets, invoices, and property descriptions. Historically, working with this text meant building complex application code: You had to export data from the database, call external model endpoints, write custom prompt wrappers, parse unpredictable responses, manage retry logic, and update database records. This application-side loop creates operational friction. It introduces query latency, bloats application code, increases model token costs, and creates data compliance risks by moving sensitive information across multiple network boundaries.

We built AlloyDB AI to bring Gemini world knowledge directly into your operational database. Rather than treating artificial intelligence as a disconnected external service, we integrated model intelligence directly into the database engine. Today, we are announcing the preview of two new SQL functions in the AlloyDB AI query engine — 

ai.classify
and 
ai.extract
— available in the 
google_ml_integration
extension (version 1.6.1 or later) on PostgreSQL 18, allowing you to perform classification and structured extraction directly inside your database using standard SQL. Supported by smart batching for AI functions (previously known as AI Function Acceleration), these functions deliver production scalability and performance. 

Now, let’s take a look at these new functions and how to use them.

Classifying text directly in SQL with ai.classify

The 

ai.classify
function categorizes text into user-defined classes without requiring manual prompt engineering. You can specify categories as a simple list of labels or provide a list containing label names and descriptions to guide model context.

Key capabilities include:

  • Single-label classification (

    output_mode => 'single'
    ) to assign the single best category

  • Multi-label classification (

    output_mode => 'multi'
    ) to return all matching categories

  • Category descriptions using 2D arrays to provide explicit context for each label

  • Few-shot prompting by supplying inline examples

  • Flexible execution modes for individual rows (

    TEXT
    ), arrays (
    TEXT[]
    ), and cursors (
    REFCURSOR
    )

Here’s a quick example showing how you can classify customer feedback directly within a SQL query:

Extracting structured JSON with ai.extract

The 

ai.extract
function transforms unstructured text into structured JSON data matching your target schema — specified as a JSON schema or a text list of fields. It handles system instructions internally, saving you from writing prompt templates or response parsers.

Key capabilities include:

  • Schema flexibility supporting standard JSON schemas or plain text field lists

  • Automatic transformation of unstructured text into machine-readable JSON

  • Overloaded function signatures for single rows, arrays, and cursor batching

Here’s an example extracting clinical fields from free-form medical notes:

Speeding up queries with smart batching

Running AI evaluations row-by-row can slow down query execution. AlloyDB addresses this with smart batching for AI functions. When you use 

ai.classify
or 
ai.extract
in SQL 
WHERE
clause expressions, the database engine automatically groups inputs into optimized micro-batches before sending them to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform models.

Smart batching delivers significant performance and efficiency improvements:

  • Faster inference for query execution compared to row-at-a-time evaluations

  • Reduces total model token spend by optimizing input prompt overhead

Real-world industry applications

Native classification and extraction functions support operational workflows across key industry sectors:

  • Healthcare: Securely convert free-text clinical notes into structured records containing patient names, symptoms, and prescribed medications, keeping patient data safely within the confines of the database.

  • Financial services: Extract vendor details, invoice dates, and line-item totals from scanned document text.

  • Legal technology: Pull governing law, liability caps, and termination notice periods from contract documents.

  • Real estate: Extract property types, bedroom counts, and price ranges from descriptive listing text.

  • Knowledge graphs: Extract entities and relationships from documents to populate PostgreSQL Property Graph (PGQ) structures.

Next steps and getting started

We are continuing to expand in-database AI capabilities in AlloyDB, with upcoming enhancements planned for advanced cost optimization, line-level provenance tracking, and query pushdowns beyond 

WHERE
clauses.

To start using 

ai.classify
and 
ai.extract
in your database:

  • Review the AlloyDB AI Query Engine documentation.

  • Explore the AlloyDB release notes.

Gary Eimerman

Ravi Rajamani

It just got easier to prove your expertise in building production-ready agents. Today, Google Cloud is introducing the Professional Agentic Architect certification as the latest milestone in our Gemini Agent Ready (GEAR) initiative. Nearly one million developers are using GEAR to skill up on agents, but what makes this particular certification so special is its adoption within Google’s walls.

Over the past four months, Google Cloud has trained thousands of forward deployed engineers and strategic partners on our own advanced curriculum. Originally built as an internal training initiative, we are now opening it up to the entire developer community and partner ecosystem through this new certification.

As the VP who manages our forward-deployed engineers here at Google Cloud (Ravi) and the managing director of Google Cloud learning (Gary), we’ve seen just how effective this program has been inside Google at helping our teams rethink the way they build, deploy, and use AI in everyday in almost every way. We’re equally about what this new certification can bring to everyone — developers, engineers, and anyone else ready to demonstrate their agentic leadership.

A new hybrid format to validate your real-world skills

This is not a traditional multiple choice exam. Google has introduced a new hybrid format that requires you to prove both conceptual know-how and hands-on execution.

  • Part 1 (The multiple choice proctored exam): Evaluates your system design choices, architectural standards, cost optimization, and security governance.

  • Part 2 (Hands-on labs on Google Skills): Puts you in an active cloud environment to build, test, and debug live agentic workflows.

Why earning this certification can help advance your career

As enterprises look to find top AI talent, this certification immediately signals that you have the advanced skills necessary to design secure, governed, and high-performance multi-agent systems.

Our research with Ipsos on AI skill building shows that certifications drive more recruiter outreach: 82% of learners using Google Skills say that mentioning Google Cloud certifications on their resume drives more recruiter responses.

And it’s not just about getting the call — it’s about being able to answer it. That same research showed that 90% of cloud professionals say credentials like Google Cloud certifications give them the verified know-how needed to fill in-demand roles.

What’s covered on the exam

The certification validates your proficiency across five key domains:

  • Build agents using low-code tools (democratizing rapid agent prototyping).

  • Use coding agents for application development (supercharging your coding productivity).

  • Develop custom agents on the Gemini platform with open source frameworks.

  • Evaluate and deploy agentic workflows (monitoring, optimizing, and ensuring performance).

  • Secure and govern agentic workflows (protecting sensitive enterprise data and ensuring model safety).

Battle-tested by thousands of Google Cloud engineers and partners — now available to you

Enterprise demand for agentic workloads has skyrocketed. As our customers move past AI prompting and run their most business critical workloads on Google Cloud, we’ve built our own team that delivers the agentic future with them — at scale. Google Cloud partners and Google’s forward deployed engineers are embedded directly with customers around the world and are prepared to solve deep technical challenges because of this rigorous curriculum and certification.

While building our forward-deployed engineering program, we wanted to standardize training and upskilling for customers, Google Cloud partners, and our own engineers with the Professional Agentic Architect certification. This ensures our own teams are using the same world-class standards that we recommend to our customers and partners, allowing us to learn from each other and sharpen our skills together.

Skill up for your certification at no cost today

  • Register for Gemini Agent Ready to get access to 35 free monthly learning credits on Google Skills. For Google Cloud customers, Get Certified provides a cohort-based, guided certification journey at no cost. 

  • For Google Cloud partners, register for Partner Certification Kickstart and review the partner learning path.

  • Review the exam guide, learning path and sample questions.

  • Get hands-on with Google Skills labs and preparation modules to get comfortable developing custom agents on Gemini platform with open source frameworks.

  • Register for the multiple-choice exam, complete the hands-on lab requirements, and claim your digital badge to showcase your expertise to the world.

Don't just prompt AI — architect it. Get certified today.

Konstantin Huneke

Co-Founder & CEO, lemonflow

Welcome back to The Blueprint, a regular feature where we highlight how Google Cloud customers are tackling unique and common challenges across industries using the latest AI and cloud technologies. We hope to inspire others looking to innovate in their work.

As the electric vehicle revolution gains steam in Europe, every charging session is a moment of truth, for the driver and for the transition itself. At lemonflow, we build AI agents purpose-built for EV charging: support agents for drivers and monitoring agents for charging networks. Our support agents answer drivers around the clock in more than 90 languages, and today they help an EV driver every 90 seconds. 

The Challenge

Before we founded lemonflow, we worked closely with leading mobility players across Europe and saw first-hand how often charging goes wrong: Between 15% and 25% of EV charging attempts in Europe end in failure. Across Europe’s rapidly expanding EV market, where battery-electric car sales grew 30% in 2025 and thousands of charge point operators run public chargers, drivers who encountered stalled charging points were often left stranded or stuck in slow call center queues.

We set out to change that hands-on: to bring the cutting edge of AI to EV charging, and to build the world’s best conversational AI for distributed hardware, an automated platform that resolves real-time charging issues via phone, chat, email, and WhatsApp. However, handling live voice support created several technical requirements:

  • Strict latency thresholds: Frustrated drivers want immediate assistance. Our testing confirmed that serving latencies above 800 milliseconds risk conversational barge-ins, causing drivers to interrupt the agent and break the interaction flow.
  • Managed API bottlenecks: Initially relying on managed LLM APIs, we faced latency deviations during peak hours (spiking from 1.0–1.2 seconds to over 1.7 seconds) and experienced HTTP 429 rate-limit errors when global usage peaked.
  • Compute-intensive conversations: Every agent works from one comprehensive prompt, paired with dynamic tool calls that read and act on live charger data. This design creates intense bursts of compute demand during calls, making throughput on shared, managed capacity difficult to guarantee under peak loads.
  • Highly fragmented ecosystem: We needed a standardized conversational engine capable of bridging around 30 distinct Charge Point Management Systems (CPMS), the backends operators use to run their chargers, each with its own APIs, data models and quirks.
  • Hundreds of tailored agents: No two operators run support the same way. Each has its own tariffs, payment methods, escalation paths and hours for human backup, and most run several agents, for example one per country, brand or hotline, with behavior that can change by time of day. Each agent’s prompt is unique and must be served at full speed and improved without breaking any of the others.

To deliver ultra-low-latency voice interactions and guaranteed serving capacity, we needed direct control over our model hosting environment.

The Solution

We wanted every driver to get best-in-class support that feels effortless, almost magical: no queue, no menu, just a short conversation that ends with the car charging. Picture a driver on a long cross-border trip, pulling into a motorway service station at 11 p.m. She plugs in, but the charger won’t start: the previous session never closed properly. She calls the number on the charger and is answered in her own language. Within seconds, our agent spots the stuck session in the charger’s logs, restarts the charger remotely and stays on the line until power is flowing.

To get there, we had to solve our latency bottlenecks and secure dedicated compute capacity. We migrated from managed APIs to self-hosting the open Gemma 4 model on Google Cloud TPU v6e hardware in the EU.

Like many startups using Gemma, the compatibility of these open models with Gemini allowed us to transition our existing prompt infrastructure with minimal modification.

Moving to self-hosted TPUs unlocked the more complete architectural control our engineering team required to establish a deterministic core layer that handles EV-specific guardrails, guards against prompt injections, and standardizes previously fragmented backend protocols into our internal format before ever reaching the LLM. Control had a second payoff: because the model and serving stack change only when we change them, every test result stays meaningful. That stability laid the foundation for Agent Coach, our background coaching engine for AI agents, described below.

We then developed an intelligent routing gateway to prioritize workloads according to operational urgency, serving live voice calls first, followed by web chats, and deferring automated re-simulations to low-traffic periods.

Custom optimizations to the open-source vLLM serving engine and memory tiering between the TPU and host memory let a single TPU slice keep many more operator agents ready for instant answers, without recalculating their context.

We also implemented automated fallback routing to self-hosted GPUs and Gemini Enterprise endpoints. Thanks to TPU reliability, Gemma answers more than 99.9% of all live conversation turns, and these fallbacks serve primarily as deployment buffers during system updates. Primary or fallback, every request is served from secure EU compute.

The Architecture

The Outcome

For the e-mobility companies we work with, and for their drivers, the result is support that simply works: our agents typically answer every call, handle more than 80% of conversations end to end without a human handover, and earn 95% driver satisfaction. Behind the scenes, self-hosting Gemma on Google Cloud TPUs transformed our performance:

  • Rapid deployment cycles: Prompt update and test cycle times dropped from 2–3 hours to about 10 minutes, a more than tenfold faster improvement loop.
  • Sub-second serving latency: We lowered our P50 latency to around 350 milliseconds and our P90 latency to around 600 milliseconds. That is roughly three times faster than our managed-API baseline and fast enough to sharply reduce customer barge-ins.
  • Zero throttling and flat latency: Dedicated TPU infrastructure eliminated HTTP 429 rate-limit errors, and latency stays flat through peak afternoon call traffic.
  • Testing without limits: On dedicated capacity, every TPU cycle that live conversations don’t need becomes testing capacity, so our team can experiment and validate at will.
  • Built for scale: Today, our agents support more than 40 charging networks in 17 countries, covering more than 250,000 charge points, around the clock. And this is just the beginning: the same platform is ready to take on many more networks and markets.

With additional compute capacity, we introduced Agent Coach, a background engine that provides agents with relevant context during live calls and turns real conversations into permanent test cases, so every call makes the next one better. We also added nightly automated regression testing across thousands of fixed conversational scenarios.

Looking ahead, we are preparing to move to Ironwood, Google’s seventh-generation TPU, as soon as it is available in our EU region. With six times the high-bandwidth memory per chip, Ironwood will multiply the number of operator agents a single TPU can keep ready in memory for instant answers.

Ultimately, our goal is that no driver is ever left stranded at a charger. They get an instant, expert answer in their own language, the charger is rebooted remotely if necessary, and our AI monitoring agents catch the next fault before another driver ever notices. Open models on dedicated Cloud TPUs give us the speed and control to make that the standard across Europe.

The Details

Our platform runs two kinds of AI agents: support agents that talk to drivers in real time, served by Gemma on Cloud TPUs for minimal latency, and monitoring agents that analyze conversations and charger logs in the background on Gemini, so operators can fix faults before the next driver is affected. To keep its core platform consistent across many kinds of e-mobility companies, from charge point operators (CPOs) and e-mobility service providers (eMSPs) to charger manufacturers, lemonflow built a translation layer that converts varied CPMS interfaces into a standardized format.

When a driver calls the support line posted on a charger, the call reaches our Conversational Engine through the operator’s own hotline. The engine then pulls the charger’s live status and Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP) logs, the messages chargers exchange with their backend, from the operator’s CPMS in real time. Because charging stations often lack digital displays, drivers are frequently unaware of underlying issues like pending mobile 3D-Secure payment authorizations, session timeouts, charging cards not enabled for roaming, power reduced by local load management, or a car that ended the session at its own charge limit. Our engine feeds structured log summaries directly into Gemma on TPU to inform interactions with drivers.

Direct model control allows us to stream token output selectively. Partial text tokens stream instantly to our Text-to-Speech (TTS) engine, while structured tool-call tokens stream asynchronously to backend systems to execute real-world actions, such as remotely restarting chargers, unlocking stuck cables, stopping sessions that failed to end, sending drivers details via SMS or email, or notifying service technicians.

Deterministic security controls screen inputs before they reach the TPU-hosted LLM, blocking malicious prompts. This architecture is designed with European critical-infrastructure requirements in mind, and it still keeps conversations snappy, with a typical response starting in around 350 milliseconds.

In the end, all of this should stay invisible to the driver: they just get a fast answer and a charger that works. We’re proud to work with Google Cloud to make that the norm and help EV adoption keep growing.
